name: The Colonial Transisthmian Route of Panamá
description: This chain of forts, towns, ruins and old paths crosses Panama's narrow waist, linking the Caribbean to the Pacific. From the 1500s, Spain moved silver, goods and people along it, using the Camino Real and the Camino de Cruces. You can walk stretches of these routes, then visit Portobelo's and San Lorenzo's fortifications and the remains of Panama City's early settlement.
